residual.wall: A displacement field is a representation, an authoring grammar, and a consumer contract. We have one 1000-float rest-radial buffer and six writers. The shatter was a consumer treating cells as faces.

question: What displacement-field techniques exist, which of them fit a locked 25×40 cage, and what is the lawful next field — not a new mesh?
coordinateSpaces: Field index: ring×40+sector. Polar UV: u=sector/40, v=ring/25. Rest-radial: + along outward normal of L. Contour: rim ring 24 → 512 radius, clamp 3.5px (goose 0.35). Screen height is a shade-only unit. Vector (unhooked): 1000×3 object/rest. Zero is +0, never 8-bit mid-gray.
physicalLaw: P' = P + h n̂  (scalar). P' = P + v  (vector). Topology unchanged.
C = Γ(L) + Σs_i. Writers add. They do not replace the cage.
A gradient of h is a normal for shade. It is not a second body.
artisticLaw: Goose is sparse RBF grain. Cellular hash meshed as tiles is crystal.
Puff is a low-order radial mode, not 1000 independent pressures.
A remote is a captured embedding or a new L. Not a photo field.

techniques.name: Scalar height along rest-radial
techniques.what: One float per cage vertex. P' = P + h n̂.

techniques.name: Tangent-space vector
techniques.what: v in (T,B,N). Travels with the walk.
techniques.have: computeLocalFrame exists on the 360. Not bound to 1000.

techniques.name: Bump / derived normal
techniques.have: deriveNormals. shadeLitMesh. Goose no longer uses it as body.

techniques.name: Microdisplacement / render tessellation
techniques.what: Renderer grows faces from a map.
techniques.have: The 1000 is the tessellation. No further grow.

techniques.name: Sparse Gaussians / RBF
techniques.what: h = Σ a_k exp(−½ r_k² / σ²).

techniques.name: Analytic primitives (rings, disks, ridges)
techniques.have: Live for brow/knit/dimple/pinches and feature layer.

techniques.name: Cellular / Worley hash
techniques.have: Still in all-script-2. Goose paint no longer calls it.
techniques.lawful: as height only — not as faces

techniques.name: Layered Σs_i
techniques.what: pressure + relief + nubs + walk + singularity + captured.
techniques.have: Additive into one buffer. No named layer stack in UI.

techniques.name: Region isolation
techniques.what: Per-organ weights / τ on the same UV.
techniques.have: Gauss on the 512 (crown/lower/sides). Not material on the 1000.

techniques.name: Baked Ptex / EXR / 8-bit height
techniques.what: Studio bake. 0.5 gray as rest is a bug.
techniques.lawful: only if resampled to 25×40 float, zero = +0

techniques.name: Divergence-free / constant-volume
techniques.have: Nothing. Pressure is a radial mode.

liveWriters: evaluateRelief → analytic + (unused cellular for goose paint)
invariants: Explore does not recut the painter.
failureModes: A second 1000×3 buffer painted beside the scalar (two bodies).
Noise as a second clock (grain walking off the walk).
uncertainty: Whether the next field the owner wants is denser RBF (more grain), vector 3D (overhang), or regional τ (organs).
Whether walkScaffoldZ should remain a writer or become a captured layer.
tests: Goose: stampGooseField, not evaluateRelief cellular, Z ≪ 400.
Puff: one radial mode, still 1000 floats.
visualConsequences: Scalar + RBF = pebbles on a pearl.
Vector 3D = undercuts, horns, a remote lip. Same count.
Volume-preserving puff = blowfish that still has mass.
implementation: Do not add a bitmap pipeline.
If Work: name the layers (Pressure / Relief / Nubs / Walk / Captured) on the same 1000. That is compose, already law.
Vector 3D is Book 009. Hook only as a replacement of the scalar, not a twin paint.
Denser goose = more RBF kernels, not cellular tiles.
